findings.summary: Table of allocate/release pairs is shown with a bare, unexplained UB column for wrong pairings, and the code appears before the idea it illustrates is named.
findings.fix: State the one-line idea first ('delete is skipped if anything between new and delete throws'), then show the code.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: double delete/use-after-free are UB, and nulling is not ownership are packed in adjacent lines, while 'Raw T* or T& = non-owning observer' mixes pointer and reference rules.
findings.evidence: Double delete and use-after-free are UB
findings.fix: Split into separate one-idea bullets (double delete; use-after-free) and keep the nullptr band-aid as its own bullet.

findings.summary: Bullet packs several ideas (move leaves source null, array specialization, delete[] and indexing) and code is shown before the ownership-handback idea is stated.
findings.evidence: unique_ptr<T[]> uses delete[] and supports p[i]
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets and put the 'release() hands the delete duty back to you' line before the code block.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas and the control-block claim is ambiguous: 'Control block thread-safe; pointee is not' is repeated, and the 'expired()' line is a fragment.
findings.evidence:
lock() gives a shared_ptr, or null if expired
expired() checks
findings.fix: Make 'expired() returns true if the object is gone' a complete bullet, and keep thread safety in one place.

findings.summary: The two-control-blocks failure is written as text where a small diagram would show it, and code for shared_from_this precedes its one-line idea.
findings.evidence:
shared_ptr<T> a(p), b(p); → two control blocks
Both delete p → double delete
findings.fix: Add a diagram of a and b each pointing to their own control block and the same object; state the shared_from_this rule before the code.

findings.summary: Code block mixes four unrelated lines with a caption explaining them afterwards, and the make_shared memory trade-off bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Object is destroyed at strong count 0, but its memory stays until the last weak_ptr dies
findings.fix: Split into two bullets (destroyed at strong 0; memory freed at weak 0) and caption each code line pair before the code, ideally as separate blocks.

findings.summary: Several bullets hold multiple ideas and the Rule-of-zero/five lines are crammed into the return-forms section.
findings.evidence:
Rule of zero: hold smart pointers or containers, write no special members
Define one of the five? Consider all (rule of five)
findings.fix: Move rules of zero and five to their own section, one idea per bullet; split 'std::move is only a cast to T&&; the move constructor does the transfer'.

findings.summary: The unique_ptr/shared_ptr comparison table is not aligned row-for-row (get() appears in both, swap/lock pair unrelated), so a skimming learner cannot compare like with like.
findings.fix: Use rows by operation (get, release/reset, count, lock) with an n/a cell where one pointer lacks it, and keep lock() under weak_ptr.
